identity.description: Attio is a CRM platform (attio.com) with a public REST API, OAuth 2.0 and API-key access, a hosted MCP server at mcp.attio.com, and webhooks.
identity.identity_notes: Docs at docs.attio.com and the MCP page at attio.com both describe the Attio product (workspace, records, lists, CRM). Matches the assigned hint attio.com.

auth.oauth_flows: Standard OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code grant with PKCE; token exchange is POST to https://app.attio.com/oauth/token. Per docs, OAuth is recommended for apps across multiple workspaces.
auth.token_refresh: unknown. The authentication guide does not state whether access tokens expire or how they are refreshed.
auth.scopes_notes: Scopes control the resources a token can access; required scopes are listed per endpoint (e.g. record_permission:read, object_configuration:read for list-records). OAuth scopes are configured in the developer console; API key scopes are set in the settings UI. Token level (workspace or user) is set via token_level on the authorize URL; user tokens are OAuth-only and require PKCE.

access.production_restrictions: Not established. Docs do not describe app review or marketplace listing requirements for OAuth apps. Apps in the App Store are said to be available on all plans.

read_ops: List records for any object (POST list-records with filter/sort, limit default 500, offset)
write_ops: Create, update, delete and view webhooks (documented as endpoints)
api.rate_limits: 100 requests/second for read requests, 25 requests/second for write requests, across the whole API; sliding-window score-based limit over 10 seconds; 429 with Retry-After on limit.
api.limitations: Official SDK status unverified; a community attio-js package says no official JS/TS SDK exists yet (unverified snippet). Write operations for core records were not directly verified beyond webhooks. The SQL endpoint is documented under a SQL tag; plan gating was reported by a third-party review but not confirmed on the vendor page. Enrichment has no API trigger per a third-party review.

claims.value: Attio is a CRM platform; docs describe a public REST API for workspace records
claims.quote: Attio provides a public REST API which exchanges JSON over HTTPS.

claims.value: API access is available on all plans including Free
claims.quote: Apps in Attio's App Store and access to Attio's API are available on all Attio plans.

claims.value: Tokens are generated by the user; API key generated in developer settings for a single workspace
claims.quote: If you only need a token for a single workspace, you can generate an API key in the developer settings page of your apps.

claims.value: OAuth 2.0 supported; Attio implements the standard OAuth 2.0 specification
claims.quote: Attio implements the standard OAuth 2.0 specification
You should prefer the OAuth 2.0 flow if building an app for multiple workspaces.

claims.value: Token sent as Bearer in Authorization header; HTTP Basic also supported
claims.quote: Pass the value of the token in the `Authorization` header of your requests like so.

claims.value: Tokens have workspace or user level; user tokens are OAuth-only and require PKCE
claims.quote: every access token has a level, which determines whose permissions the token acts with.

claims.value: Scopes control resource access; required scopes listed per endpoint
claims.quote: use scopes to control the resources that the token has access to.

claims.value: 100 req/s read, 25 req/s write, across the whole API
claims.quote: Our rate limit across the whole API is 100 requests per second for read requests, 25 requests per second for write requests.
Rate limit responses always have the HTTP status code `429`.

claims.value: Webhooks creatable in settings UI or via API; endpoints for create/update/delete/view
claims.quote: There are two places you can create webhooks: in our settings pages, and the API.

claims.value: Attio-Signature is SHA256 HMAC of the request body using the webhook secret
claims.quote: The `Attio-Signature` value is calculated using a SHA256 HMAC of the request body using your webhook secret as the secret.

claims.value: Records list endpoint works across all objects and supports filter/sort/limit/offset; OpenAPI tags include Notes, Tasks, Lists, Meetings, Webhooks, etc.
claims.quote: Lists people, company or other records, with the option to filter and sort results.

claims.value: Attio hosts its own MCP server at https://mcp.attio.com/mcp
claims.quote: Any other MCP client can connect using the custom connector URL, https://mcp.attio.com/mcp.

claims.value: kesslerio/attio-mcp-server (Apache 2.0, also on npm as attio-mcp-server) is third-party

open_questions: Whether access tokens expire and how refresh works (not stated in the auth guide).
Whether creating an OAuth app or API key in developer settings requires workspace admin rights (admin_approval_required unknown).
Whether a trial or sandbox workspace is needed for testing; not established.
Official SDK status: no first-party JS/TS SDK was confirmed; a PyPI package named attio appeared but its owner was not verified.
Whether OAuth apps need Attio app review before public listing; not established.
Full list of webhook event types was not retrieved (V2 list-entry events and note.created were mentioned).
Plan gating for the SQL endpoint: a third-party review says it is plan-gated, but the vendor plans page only lists the SQL query workflow block, and its plan placement is unclear.
Community MCP server kesslerio/attio-mcp-server was only seen in search results; its README and maintainer were not fetched. A hmk/attio-mcp-server fork also appears on directory sites.

assessment.approach: Wrap/benchmark vendor's official MCP server; add managed auth
rationale: Self-serve test credentials (free self serve) and a documented REST interface.
